PullRequest.Title: sessions: Soften side-by-side session dividers
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #338678. ## Summary - Keep a subtle divider visible between sessions at rest by using the themed panel border at half opacity, rather than removing it completely. - Preserve the full-strength `contrastBorder` when defined, existing hover/drag feedback, the outer card border, and the separate chat-group dividers. - Add a two-visible-sessions component fixture in dark, light, and both high-contrast themes, plus regression coverage for theme changes and translucent border colors. ## Validation Validated with Node.js 24.18.0 after updating the branch to current `main`. - `npm run compile-client` - passed. - `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionsPart.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionGridLayout.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/agentsPartCard.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileSessionsPart.test.ts` - passed, 48 tests. - `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/sessionsPart.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionsPart.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsGrid.fixture.ts` - passed. - `git diff --check` - passed. Visual validation during implementation: all 12 session-grid fixtures rendered without errors; dark/light side-by-side screenshots were stable. Browser checks verified the resting divider in all four themes, stronger hover/drag feedback, and an 80px drag resizing both session panes while retaining the subtle divider afterward. ## Manual testing 1. Open two sessions side by side in the Agents Window. 2. Check that the resting divider remains visible but quieter than the surrounding panel chrome in dark and light themes. 3. Hover over and drag the boundary; the sash should highlight and both panes should resize normally. 4. Switch to either high-contrast theme and check that the divider retains the full-strength contrast border. ## Screenshots Before/after PNGs are prepared locally and will be uploaded by the author after PR creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or theme-switch an Agents Window containing side-by-side sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsPart creation or IThemeService color-theme notification synchronously calls updateStyles, applies card CSS variables, computes the separator Color, and walks the existing grid branches to update separator class/style properties. This completes before the refreshed divider is displayed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The existing grid style walk scales with the number of nested split branches created by visible sessions; the changed color operation is one Color/RGBA allocation per SessionsPart style update, independent of session count. Theme changes are infrequent rather than per-frame or per-input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous renderer-thread update; no queue, parallel work, limiter, or overlapping asynchronous operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme colors are resolved from the current theme on each existing style update. The diff neither adds nor defeats a cache; warm and cold behavior differ only in already-existing theme-service state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed getter and the complete updateStyles-to-Grid.style-to-branch recursion were traced. The recursive DOM writes already occurred before the diff; only contrast-color precedence and a constant-time alpha transformation changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact grid depth varies with visible session layout, but the diff does not change the number of branches, DOM writes, or update frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The same synchronous style walk and DOM property writes occur before and after; the added constant-size color allocation on part creation/theme changes is not a realistic latency, CPU, GC, rendering, or layout regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load the sessions grid component-fixture gallery and render the new SideBySide variants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Playwright test performs one local gallery navigation, then the fixture explorer eagerly mounts all grid variants and waits for the increased DOM counts. Each new SideBySide theme variant creates two mocked sessions and renders two chat widgets before the gallery assertions can pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate once to the local component-fixture explorer and wait for network idle
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local page navigation per test, unchanged by the diff; the returned page now mounts 12 rather than 8 fixture variants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same test made one local gallery navigation and mounted 8 variants at a 3400x4600 viewport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The local navigation and all fixture mounts must complete before locator-count assertions; the diff increases in-page test rendering but does not add another network request boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The gallery intentionally grows from 8 to 12 fixture mounts and from 20 to 28 visible session views; the new fixture itself expands across dark, light, and two high-contrast variants.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within each fixture, chat rendering uses Promise.all for its two mocked chat views. The gallery mounts all registered variants through existing fixture-explorer behavior; no production concurrency or external-service burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixture registration and mounting do not use a data cache. All sessions and chats are in-memory mocks, so there are no cold/warm remote cache misses or negative-cache retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the fixture definitions, two-chat mocked render path, increased expected counts, larger viewport, and single local navigation are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CI time and memory increase are not quantified, and generic fixture tooling may add incidental asset requests, but there is no product path and no evidence of an unbounded or severe test-throughput regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance issue. The bounded 4-variant/8-session-view increase is intentional test-only visual coverage, uses mocks rather than production network or filesystem services, and does not affect application users.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced the runtime theme-update DOM path and the fixture-gallery expansion; no high-confidence, actionable product performance regression was introduced.
